sections.title: Introduction: The Dimensional Paradox
lecture_lines: Can a 1D line fill a 2D square?
A space-filling curve traverses every point.
Imagine a vacuum cleaning a room.
animations: Fade in title: The Dimensional Paradox (#FFFFFF).
Show a point (#00FF00) and a line (#FF00FF).
Morph point into a 2D square shape (#FFFF00) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vacuum.svg].

sections.title: The Mechanism: Recursive Construction
lecture_lines: We use recursive construction for complexity.
Start with a simple generator shape.
Iteratively replace segments to fill space.

sections.title: Visualizing the Mapping (1D to 2D)
lecture_lines: As iterations increase, the curve densifies.
A single thread covers the entire plane.
Infinite iterations result in a filled square.
Dimensions collapse into a continuous path.
animations: Draw a 1D line with segments (#FFFF00) represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thread.svg].
Fold the line into a 2D space (#FF00FF).
Show filled square result (#00FFFF) created from the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thread.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: They are infinitely long yet continuous.
Complexity emerges from simple recursive rules.
